title: Loss of the tumor suppressor p53 generates a signaling gradient that drives epithelial clonal expansion.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both processed files in GEO series GSE275726 (the only deposit tied to this lab/paper): GSE275726_Combined_Peaks_WT.bed.gz (1,668 rows) and GSE275726_Combined_Peaks_3KR.bed.gz (6,753 rows). Both are 5-column BED of 1-base-pair peak summits on mouse genome build mm10 with one unnamed numeric score (WT range 2.76-294.60, 3KR 2.53-275.23); no header, no units, no bound/unbound label, no replicate-level files. 53.1% of WT summits fall within 200 bp of a 3KR summit. Read all six GEO sample records (3 p53WT, 3 p53-3KR ChIP-seq libraries, no input/IgG controls, peaks called by MACS2 on reads pooled across the 3 replicates). Confirmed the Science article page returns HTTP 403, Europe PMC has no full text or supplement, and Zenodo/DataCite searches on the DOI return zero records. Searched GEO for companion RNA-seq, screen or imaging deposits (several query sets, plus all 2025-2026 p53/skin series and all 21 series from senior author Beronja) and found none.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything beyond the ChIP-seq peak files: the radial Wnt-activity gradient, the single-cell Wnt imaging, the clonal-expansion measurements, and the genetic screen of >1,000 candidate p53-regulated genes are known only from the abstract and press coverage. No peak counts, screen scores or expression values could be compared against the paper because the full text and supplementary tables are paywalled.

a1_downloadable.note: Both peak files downloaded anonymously from the GEO FTP site in seconds (22 KB + 70 KB compressed); no login or application. Raw reads are in SRA (SRX25837659-64) but fastq is out of scope.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The files are a positives-only list of 8,421 peak summits. There is no bound/unbound column: the negative class would have to be invented by sampling background genome regions, and the only numeric column is an unlabelled peak-caller score. Verified by parsing both files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Only mm10 coordinates are given; the DNA sequence a model would read is absent and must be cut out of a separate 2.6 GB mouse reference genome. That is one download, not thousands of lookups, so this is a soft fail, not the decisive one.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL. Column 5 has no name and no documentation anywhere in the GEO record; it is presumably a MACS2 (peak-calling software) score but whether it is fold-enrichment or -log10 of a q-value is unstated, so any regression on peak strength has undefined units.

a5_enough_rows.note: 1,668 WT + 6,753 3KR summits counted in the files. Enough rows for a classifier in principle, but the biological unit is 2 conditions x 3 pooled replicates, and peaks were called on pooled reads so there is no replicate-level table.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.09 GB of peak files; ~2.6 GB if the mm10 reference genome is added
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized. Verified file sizes on disk.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: the Science paper is paywalled, has no PubMed Central record and no retrievable supplement, so the 1,668 / 6,753 peak counts cannot be compared with any number the authors published.

a8_label_provenance.note: Peaks are MACS2 output from a physical chromatin immunoprecipitation measurement, not another predictive model's output, and are not computed from DNA sequence features, so there is no circularity. They are, however, threshold-dependent calls with no input/IgG control samples deposited.

existing_models.name: BPNet (Avsec et al., Nature Genetics 2021), a convolutional neural network that predicts base-resolution transcription-factor binding profiles from DNA sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported in the paper's abstract and follow-ups as evaluated on held-out chromosomes (chr1, chr8, chr9) with profile likelihood and Jensen-Shannon divergence metrics; exact numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cooperative 'soft motif syntax' between factors, and transfer of learned syntax to new cell types, are named as open.

existing_models.name: ChromBPNet (2025), a bias-corrected base-resolution model of chromatin accessibility and factor footprints
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked against Enformer on variant-effect prioritisation with held-out chromosome splits; numbers not retrieved in detail.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Separating enzyme/sequence bias from true factor footprints, and cross-cell-type generalisation.

existing_models.name: Enformer / Borzoi / AlphaGenome, long-context sequence-to-function models that predict many genomic tracks from DNA
existing_models.score_and_split: Standard evaluation is held-out chromosomes on human and mouse ENCODE tracks; AlphaGenome weights released under a non-commercial licence.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: All are trained on one reference genome and a fixed track set, so performance on new assays, tissues and individuals is explicitly open.

existing_models.name: deepTFBS (2025), multi-task and transfer-learning model for within- and cross-species transcription-factor binding site prediction
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to improve cross-species binding-site prediction; split and numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-species transfer with few training peaks.

existing_models.name: p53-specific logistic regression using sequence plus chromatin modification data (PubMed 23599002, 'Models incorporating chromatin modification data identify functionally important p53 binding sites')
existing_models.score_and_split: Numbers not retrieved; a 2013 regression model on human p53 ChIP data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which bound sites are functional rather than merely occupied.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA language models), with a frozen trunk and a logistic-regression head on embeddings of 500 bp windows around each summit
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; ~17k windows (positives plus matched negatives) is a few CPU-hours of embedding
backbone.licence: DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer weights are openly downloadable; AlphaGenome weights are non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: ReMap / ENCODE p53 (TP53) ChIP-seq peak collections across human and mouse cell types, plus mouse ENCODE epidermal chromatin accessibility
integration.join_key: mm10 genomic coordinates (with liftOver to hg38 for the human sets)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Are the p53 sites used in adult epidermal basal progenitors a tissue-specific subset of the general p53 cistrome, and does the acetylation-defective 3KR mutant simply keep the strongest canonical sites or reach a different set? — answerable in principle, but not with 90 KB of summit coordinates lacking signal tracks or controls.

controls.positive_control: The canonical p53 response-element motif should be strongly enriched in the summits versus GC-matched background, and known targets (Cdkn1a/p21, Mdm2) should carry peaks; this is checkable but requires the mm10 genome, which I did not download.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle bound/unbound labels and confirm collapse to chance; also compare against a motif-only position-weight-matrix scan, which for p53 is already a strong classifier.
controls.external_validation: Independent p53 ChIP-seq in other mouse tissues via ReMap/ENCODE, or human p53 peaks lifted over — exists, but was not opened here.

honest_claim_h3: A model built on this deposit could claim only: 'DNA sequence around 8,421 MACS2 summit calls from one lab's pooled p53 ChIP-seq in mouse epidermal basal progenitors separates those summits from background genome better/worse than a p53 motif scan' — it says nothing about the paper's actual finding, the Wnt gradient driving clonal expansion, because none of that data is public.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence to predict where the p53 protein binds in mouse skin progenitor cells.
plain_idea.train_on: 500 base-pair windows of mouse genome (build mm10) around each measured binding-site summit, against background windows sampled to match base composition; 8,421 measured summits were counted in the files (1,668 from normal p53, 6,753 from the acetylation-defective 3KR mutant).
plain_idea.predict: A bound/not-bound call (or a binding-strength score) per genomic window. The true answer comes from chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (pulling down p53 with an antibody and sequencing the attached DNA), processed with the MACS2 peak caller on reads pooled across three mice per genotype.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: In principle it would say which sequence features mark the p53 sites that stay occupied in a self-renewing tissue; in practice the question is already covered by open sequence-to-function models, and the paper's distinctive measurements are not public.

more_or_better_data.why: 8,421 summit coordinates from one mouse tissue is tiny next to the hundreds of ENCODE/ReMap transcription-factor datasets that BPNet, ChromBPNet, Enformer and Borzoi train on, and we have no signal tracks, only called peaks.

confidence_score.why: Peaks were called on reads pooled across the three replicates, so the deposit contains no replicate-level data from which to estimate measurement noise or per-site confidence.

models_beatable.why: The relevant models are 2021-2025, convolutional or long-context transformer architectures, and are already evaluated on held-out chromosomes; and for p53 specifically a plain motif scan is a strong baseline, so there is little headroom to claim.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data joins to this that would make improvement near-certain: we cannot run the existing models on exactly this label (different assay processing, no control track), and the evaluation split would not match theirs.

ml_idea: Predict p53 occupancy in mouse epidermal basal progenitors from DNA sequence (frozen DNA language model plus a head, positives = the 8,421 deposited summits, negatives = composition-matched background, held-out chromosomes as the split), optionally classifying which sites are retained by the acetylation-defective 3KR mutant. Rejected: positives-only data, undocumented score units, a confounded WT-versus-3KR comparison, and a field already served by open, honestly evaluated models.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~17k windows of 500 bp through a small DNA language model on CPU at roughly 1-2 windows/second per core; the only large item is the 2.6 GB mm10 reference genome, which I did not download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows and columns of the two BED files — done: 1,668 and 6,753 one-base-pair summits, five unnamed columns, no bound/unbound label and no replicate-level or control data.

verdict_reason: The only public data for this Science paper is a 2024 GEO deposit (GSE275726) of two peak-summit BED files totalling 90 KB: 1,668 wild-type and 6,753 p53-3KR summits with one undocumented score column, no negatives, no sequences, no input controls and no replicate-level calls (A2, A4 fail; A3, A7 soft fails). Everything the paper is actually about — the radial Wnt-activity gradient, single-cell Wnt imaging, clonal-expansion rates and the >1,000-gene in vivo genetic screen — has no deposit anywhere I could find (GEO, Zenodo, DataCite) and the article itself is paywalled with no PubMed Central record. The residual project, predicting p53 binding from DNA sequence, is served by open, honestly evaluated models (BPNet, ChromBPNet, Enformer/Borzoi/AlphaGenome) and by a plain p53 motif scan. A further file-level red flag: the 3KR peaks are named '3KR_Doxo' (doxorubicin) while the GEO protocol describes Nutlin-3a stabilisation, so a wild-type-versus-mutant comparison would be confounded by treatment.
